issues.t: Head gasket leak on the 4.5L six
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, the temperature gauge creeps up when towing or climbing, white exhaust smoke, or oil that looks milky.
issues.why: Head gaskets are a known weak spot on the 4.5L six at higher mileage, and the cylinder head can warp if the engine has ever overheated.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Ask a shop for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas (block) test before more damage is done.

issues.t: Front axle knuckle seals leak grease or gear oil
issues.sym: Greasy, dirt-caked buildup on the round steering knuckles behind the front wheels, or runny oil dripping from them.
issues.why: The seals around the front steering knuckles wear out with age and miles. Thick buildup usually means the inner knuckle seal has failed; thin oil can mean differential oil is getting past the axle seal.
issues.next: Have the front knuckles inspected. A knuckle rebuild with new seals and fresh grease stops the leak and protects the wheel bearings and front axle joints.

issues.t: Rusted heater pipe leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant smell, a small coolant puddle at the back of the engine, or a slowly falling coolant level.
issues.why: A steel heater pipe runs from the thermostat housing toward the firewall. On these older trucks it rusts through, along with its rubber hoses.
issues.next: Have the back of the engine checked for coolant leaks. Replacing the pipe and hoses is often paired with a water pump and radiator flush since the system is already drained.

issues.t: Power steering leaks from the reservoir or pump
issues.sym: Reddish fluid on the engine or ground near the front, a whining sound when turning, or steering that feels heavier.
issues.why: Power steering leaks are common on older Land Cruisers. The reservoir seals are often the culprit, and the pump can start leaking at high mileage.
issues.next: Check the reservoir lid and top plate seals first; they are simple parts. If the pump or steering box is leaking, have it repaired before it runs low and gets damaged.

issues.t: Water leaks from clogged sunroof drains
issues.sym: Wet headliner, damp carpets or water dripping inside after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog with dirt and debris, so water overflows into the cabin. The trim below the sliding rear side windows can also let water in.
issues.next: Clear the drain tubes with compressed air or a flexible line, and check the window trim seals. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Frame cracks near the steering box
issues.sym: Steering that feels loose or vague, or visible cracks in the frame around where the steering box bolts on.
issues.why: Bigger, heavier tires put more load on the frame where the steering box mounts, and the metal can crack there over time.
issues.next: Have the frame around the steering box inspected, especially on a lifted truck. Cracks can be welded and reinforced with a plate.

issues.t: Rust on the rear body, tailgate and frame
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes along the rear sills, wheel arches, around the tailgate and window seams, or flaky rust on the rear frame.
issues.why: Road salt and coastal air eat into these areas on older Land Cruisers, especially trucks that towed boats or were driven in snow states.
issues.next: Inspect the underside and body seams once a year. Treat surface rust early; badly rotted frame or body sections need a body shop.

issues.t: Brake booster or ABS pump fails and the pedal goes hard
issues.sym: A buzzer and brake/ABS warning lights, a whining noise from the brake unit, then a brake pedal that needs much more force or sinks far down.
issues.why: These trucks use a hydraulic brake booster and ABS actuator instead of a vacuum booster. The pump, accumulator or actuator can wear out, cutting brake assist.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. A scan for ABS codes will show whether the booster pump, accumulator or actuator is at fault.

issues.t: Timing belt and water pump past due
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A worn belt can snap and the engine suddenly stops and won't restart. A leaking water pump may show coolant at the front of the engine first.
issues.why: The 4.7L V8 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule, together with the water pump it drives. Many used trucks have missed this service.
issues.next: If there is no record of it, have the timing belt, water pump, tensioner and idlers replaced. Roughly every 90,000 to 100,000 miles is the usual interval.

issues.t: Height control suspension sags or rides hard
issues.sym: A bouncy or harsh ride, the front end sitting low, the truck not changing height, or a suspension warning light.
issues.why: Trucks with Active Height Control use hydraulic fluid and nitrogen-filled spheres in place of normal springs. The spheres lose charge with age, and the system can leak. The later KDSS system can also leak at its valves.
issues.next: Have a shop that knows Land Cruisers check the fluid and sphere pressures. Refreshing the spheres and fluid often fixes it; some owners convert to regular springs.

issues.t: Torque converter failure on the 4-speed automatic
issues.sym: Shudder at steady speeds, slipping, flaring revs or harsh shifts, sometimes followed by loss of drive.
issues.why: The torque converter in the earlier 4-speed automatic is a known failure point on these trucks.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and get a transmission diagnosis early. A fluid service can help a mild shudder, but a failed converter has to be replaced.

issues.t: Front CV joints click when turning
issues.sym: Clicking or knocking from the front wheels when pulling away or turning at full lock.
issues.why: The outer joints on the front drive shafts wear out, especially if a split boot let dirt and water in.
issues.next: Look for torn rubber boots behind the front wheels. Replace the worn drive shaft before the joint breaks.

issues.t: Plastic heater hose tees crack and leak coolant
issues.sym: Sweet coolant smell, coolant on top of the engine or under the truck, or the heater blowing cold. A failed heater core can fog the windows.
issues.why: Plastic T-fittings in the heater hoses get brittle with heat and age and crack. Heater cores can also leak with age.
issues.next: Replace the plastic tees with metal or new factory parts before they break, and check the heater hoses at the same time.

issues.t: Power steering hoses and rack leak
issues.sym: Power steering fluid low or on the ground, a whine when turning, or a damp steering rack.
issues.why: The return hoses from the reservoir and the rack seals harden with age and start to seep.
issues.next: Top up and find the source. Hoses are a simple fix; a leaking rack may need resealing or replacing.

issues.t: Starter clicks but won't crank
issues.sym: A single click or nothing at all when you turn the key or press start, often more often when hot, with a good battery.
issues.why: The contacts inside the starter wear out on the V8 trucks, and starters on these Land Cruisers fail at higher mileage. On the V8s the starter sits under the intake, so it is a big job.
issues.next: Have the battery and connections tested first. If the starter is at fault, replace it or, on the 4.7L, have the starter contacts renewed.

issues.t: Secondary air injection pump or valve failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with flashing 4WD or traction lights and reduced power right after a cold start.
issues.why: A small air pump blows air into the exhaust for a few seconds on cold starts to cut emissions. Moisture gets into the pump and its valves, and they corrode and fail.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The truck usually drives fine, but replace the failed pump or valve so emissions and stability systems work normally.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may deploy on their own (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The curtain airbags could go off on rough terrain without a crash.
issues.why: The airbag control module was programmed in a way that could misread certain jolts as a rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A Toyota dealer replaces the airbag control module for free.

issues.t: Blue smoke and burning oil
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke from the tailpipe, especially at startup, and needing to add oil between changes.
issues.why: Owners report worn valve stem seals or piston rings letting oil into the cylinders at moderate mileage, and repairs can be major.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and track how much it uses. Have a compression and leak-down test to see whether it is seals or rings.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Pink coolant drips at the front of the truck, a falling coolant level, or the temperature rising when towing.
issues.why: The plastic radiator tanks crack with age and heat. In a large owner poll it was the most common repair on these trucks.
issues.next: Check the radiator seams for pink crust or drips. Replace the radiator before it fails on the road, and do not drive if it overheats.

issues.t: Water pump leaks
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a dried pink crust near the pump, or a slowly dropping coolant level.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out and starts to weep. It was the second most common repair in an owner poll.
issues.next: Have it replaced when you see it leaking, along with the drive belt and thermostat if they are old.

issues.t: Coolant leak from the valley plate at the back of the engine
issues.sym: A coolant drip at the back of the engine near the transmission, coolant smell, and a slowly dropping level.
issues.why: A coolant passage plate sits in the valley between the cylinder banks. Its seal can fail, letting coolant run down the back of the engine.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm where the leak is coming from. The intake has to come off, so it makes sense to replace other aging seals at the same time.

issues.t: Cam tower and timing cover oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil seeping down the sides or front of the engine, burning oil smell, or drips under the truck.
issues.why: The sealant between the camshaft housings and cylinder heads, and around the timing cover, can break down over time.
issues.next: Small seeps can be watched. If it is dripping onto the exhaust, have it resealed; it is many hours of labor, so ask about doing the valley plate and water pump at the same time.

issues.t: Clunk from the driveshaft when stopping or pulling away
issues.sym: A slight jolt as you come to a stop, then a clunk from under the truck when you pull away.
issues.why: The universal joints and slip joint on the driveshafts lose their grease, especially after water crossings or off-road use, and start to bind.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft joints greased. If the clunk continues, the U-joints may need replacing.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt sensor wire can break and turn off airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, or the passenger airbag 'off' light may show with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A wiring harness for the front passenger seat belt tension sensor can wear and break, switching off the passenger front, knee and seat side airbags.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A Toyota dealer modifies or replaces the passenger seat belt assembly for free.

issues.t: Wrong front airbag may have been installed (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign.
issues.why: Some trucks may have the wrong driver or front passenger airbag fitted, which may not deploy as designed in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A Toyota dealer replaces the affected airbags for free.

issues.t: Rough or harsh shifting
issues.sym: Hard or clunky shifts, especially at low speeds, on a fairly new truck.
issues.why: Owners report harsh shifts from the 8-speed automatic early in ownership; the cause is often the transmission's learned shift settings or software.
issues.next: Check the fluid and ask a dealer to scan for codes and check for software updates or a reset of the shift learning.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal when backing up
issues.sym: A loud squeal or metal-on-metal sound from the front brakes when reversing, often worst on the first stops after the truck has sat.
issues.why: The pads and anti-squeal shims are not damping vibration well. Toyota issued bulletins with new pads, shims, springs and grease to fix it.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer about the front brake squeal service bulletins (T-SB-0046-25 and T-SB-0006-26). The repair is covered for 3 years or 36,000 miles.

issues.t: Fuel tube near the tank can come apart and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Gas smell around the truck, drips under the rear, or the engine losing power.
issues.why: A plastic fuel tube connection near the fuel tank may disconnect, letting fuel leak out, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell gas, park it outside and have it towed. Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers inspect the joint and add a clamp or replace the tube for free.

issues.t: Gauge screen can stay partly blank at startup (recall)
issues.sym: Parts of the digital gauge display stay blank after you start the truck, so warning lights for oil pressure, engine temperature or charging may not show.
issues.why: Two startup programs in the instrument cluster software can overlap and leave sections of the screen empty.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls. A Toyota dealer updates the gauge cluster software for free.

issues.t: Backup camera can freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera picture freezes or the screen stays blank.
issues.why: A software error in the parking assist system can stop the rear camera image from showing.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look behind you until it is fixed. Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers update the software for free.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky downshifts when slowing
issues.sym: The truck lunges or jolts as it downshifts while slowing down, or engages hard when you accelerate again.
issues.why: Owners report rough shift behavior from the 8-speed hybrid transmission; dealers often cannot reproduce it and no fix has been announced.
issues.next: Note when it happens (speed, temperature, braking or coasting) and have a dealer road test it and check for software updates.

issues.t: Transmission oil pump failure and limp mode
issues.sym: Screeching during shifts, loss of power or the truck going into limp mode with transmission warning messages.
issues.why: A few owners report the transmission's electric oil pump failing early. Some dealers replaced the whole transmission because the pump was not sold separately.
issues.next: Stop driving if it goes into limp mode and have it towed to a dealer. This should be covered by the powertrain warranty.

issues.t: Sunroof or side glass shatters
issues.sym: A loud bang and shattered sunroof or window glass, sometimes while driving with no visible impact.
issues.why: Owners have reported glass breaking suddenly. The cause has not been confirmed and there is no recall.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Report it to Toyota and NHTSA, and ask your dealer or insurer about replacement.
